name: Sock press change, refining and doré pour (one smelt batch)
summary: The mill's gold ends up in two places: zinc precipitate caught in the sock presses of the Merrill-Crowe circuit, and gravity concentrate from the shaking table. This process takes each batch into the restricted refinery, burns the press socks to ash or dries and cleans the concentrate, smelts it with flux and pours numbered doré bars into the vault. One gold room operator on day shift does most of the work, with a security officer and the mill superintendent witnessing entries, pours and weights. Batches wait for refinery days and overnight burns, and every handling step is a theft risk that needs two people and camera coverage.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian underground gold producer whose gravity and Merrill-Crowe mill produces about 7,500 to 8,500 oz a month, with a small on-site refinery run by one operator per rotation.
baseline.notes: One case is one smelt batch: either a sock press change (about every two weeks) or a week's table concentrate.

unit_of_work: one smelt and pour batch (precipitate or table concentrate)
trigger: A sock press is due for change, or a week of shaking table concentrate is in the refinery vault.
end_state: The precipitate or concentrate has been smelted into numbered, weighed and sampled doré bars locked in the vault with a signed register, and the standby press is ready.

volume.seasonality: Steady; the table concentrate share follows the share of Eagle underground ore, since Mishi ore bypasses the gravity circuit.

evidence.note: Socks removed bi-weekly (about 2 batches a month) and table concentrate upgraded daily (er2022); weekly table concentrate smelts (about 4 a month) are the author's assumption.

Two operators on rotation (organisation file), one on site on day shift; press changes, burns, smelts and records take most of their time, with the rest on table concentrate custody and refinery housekeeping.

roles.title: Mill process and control room operator

evidence.note: Merrill-Crowe operator isolates and re-socks the press.
Refinery entry, escorts, pours and camera review.
Pour reconciliation.
Witness signature and investigations.

systems.name: Mill distributed control system and process historian
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Gate access, camp booking and gold room access logs
Incident, inspection and training records system

resources.name: Refinery (sock burner oven and propane furnace in a secure room)

steps.name: Open the refinery under two-person entry
steps.description: On a scheduled refinery day the security officer and the gold room operator open the restricted refinery together with their own keys or cards, check the alarm panel and CCTV, and record the entry time and names in the access log.

control.basis: Gold room security procedure: restricted two-person entry, CCTV recording, gold-bearing material never left unattended

next.condition: a sock press is due for change
a week of table concentrate is ready to smelt

evidence.note: The refinery is a restricted-entry facility with CCTV and a concrete vault (er2022); double-locked entry with card passes (goldroom911). Socks are changed bi-weekly (er2022) and table concentrate is assumed to be smelted weekly, giving the 1:2 split.

steps.name: Take the loaded sock press off line
steps.description: When the press is due, the Merrill-Crowe operator switches the precipitate flow to the standby sock press, drains and air-blows the loaded press, locks out its feed pump and valves and checks the press is depressurised before it is opened.

error.defect_description: Press opened with residual pressure or solution, spraying cyanide.

control.basis: Lockout and tagging before opening a pressure filter (Ontario Regulation 854 under the OHSA; site lockout procedure)

evidence.note: Two sock presses in parallel with one on standby; socks removed bi-weekly (er2022). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Strip the loaded socks under escort
steps.description: The gold room operator opens the press, pulls each precipitate-laden sock off its frame, bags it and loads the bags into a locked cart while the security officer stands by and the camera records, then both escort the cart to the refinery.

error.defect_description: A sock is torn and precipitate is spilled in the press area.

control.basis: Gold room security procedure: restricted two-person entry, CCTV recording, gold-bearing material never left unattended

evidence.note: Socks are removed and sent to the refinery (er2022); precipitate must never be left unattended (goldroom911). Time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-sock and precoat the press
steps.description: The Merrill-Crowe operator fits clean socks to the frames, closes the press, precoats it with Dicalite slurry, pressure-tests it, removes the lockout and leaves it as the standby press.

error.defect_description: Sock poorly seated, letting precipitate through to barren solution on the next run.

control.basis: Lockout and tagging before opening a pressure filter (Ontario Regulation 854 under the OHSA; site lockout procedure)

evidence.note: Sock press primed with Dicalite (er2022). Time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Burn the socks in the sock burner oven
steps.description: In the refinery the gold room operator loads the bagged socks into trays, puts them in the sock burner oven and starts the burn cycle that removes the cloth and filter aid, leaving gold and silver precipitate ash; the oven is locked and runs overnight.

error.defect_description: Burn too hot or too short, leaving cloth that fouls the smelt.

control.basis: Refinery emission sources operated under the mill's air Environmental Compliance Approval (Environmental Protection Act, Ontario)

evidence.note: Solids-laden press socks are burned in a sock burner oven to remove cloth and filter aid (er2022); the mill holds an air approval for the bullion furnace and other sources (ero1400). Burn duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Dry the table concentrate
steps.description: The gold room operator takes the week's locked canisters of shaking table concentrate from the vault, checks each canister seal and weight against the transfer sheets, and dries the concentrate in trays in the refinery oven.

error.defect_description: A canister weight differs from its transfer sheet and is not flagged.

evidence.note: Gravity concentrate is upgraded on a shaking table daily and sent to the refinery (er2022). Weekly smelting and drying time are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Remove magnetics from the table concentrate
steps.description: The operator passes the dry concentrate under a hand or drum magnet to pull out steel from grinding media and liners, re-weighs the cleaned concentrate and the magnetics, and keeps the magnetics for re-treatment in the mill.

error.defect_description: Steel left in the concentrate, making a dirty, low-grade pour.

evidence.note: Table concentrate is treated by magnetic separation before smelting (er2022).

steps.name: Weigh the concentrate and mix the flux
steps.description: The operator weighs the cooled precipitate ash or cleaned table concentrate on the refinery scale, calculates a flux charge of borax, sodium nitrate, silica sand, soda ash and manganese dioxide from the refinery recipe, mixes it in, and writes the weights in the gold room book.

error.defect_description: Weight mis-recorded or flux ratio wrong, giving a dirty pour.

evidence.note: Smelting reagents borax, sodium nitrate, soda ash, silica sand and manganese dioxide (er2022); the gold room book records weights and conversions (goldroom911). The wait covers the overnight burn or drying and cooling.

steps.name: Smelt the charge in the furnace
steps.description: The operator loads the charge into the crucible of the propane-fired Wabi furnace, brings it to temperature, stirs and skims as the flux melts, and watches the fume extraction, wearing aluminised PPE and a face shield.

error.defect_description: Crucible failure or boil-over loses metal into the furnace lining.

control.basis: Furnace and molten metal procedure; bullion furnace operated under the mill's air Environmental Compliance Approval

evidence.note: Smelting in a Wabi furnace fuelled by propane, table concentrate and sock ash smelted separately (er2022); bullion furnace replaced under an amended air approval in December 2020 (ero1400). Smelt time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pour the doré into moulds
steps.description: With the security officer watching, the operator tilts the furnace and pours the molten bullion into a cascade of preheated moulds, letting slag overflow into the last mould, and leaves the bars to cool.

control.basis: Gold room security procedure: restricted two-person entry, CCTV recording, gold-bearing material never left unattended; very few people told of pour times

evidence.note: Very few people should be aware of gold pours (goldroom911).

steps.name: Clean, weigh and stamp the bars
steps.description: When the bars are cool the operator knocks off the slag, quenches and wire-brushes each bar, weighs it on the certified scale, stamps a bar number and the date, and records the gross weight in the gold room book.

evidence.note: Doré of 80 to 94% gold (er2022). Finishing time is the author's estimate; cooling is the wait.

steps.name: Take drill samples from each bar
steps.description: The operator drills a top and bottom sample from each bar, bags the turnings with the bar number and puts them in the locked sample box for the site assay of gold and silver, which estimates content before the refiner's outturn.

error.defect_description: Sample bag carries the wrong bar number.

evidence.note: Site bar sampling before refinery settlement is common practice; the organisation file has no link from this process to mill-assay-lab.

steps.name: Witness weights and sign the bar register
steps.description: The mill superintendent re-weighs a sample of the bars, checks the numbers and weights in the gold room book against the scale and signs the bar register with the gold room operator.

control.basis: Gold control procedure: a manager independent of the refinery witnesses and signs bar weights

evidence.note: Independent witness of bar weights is common gold control practice; author's estimate.

steps.name: Lock the bars in the vault and close the refinery
steps.description: The security officer and operator place the bars in the vault safe, lock it with both keys, set the alarm, sign out of the refinery and note the vault count in the security log.

control.basis: Gold room security procedure: restricted two-person entry, CCTV recording, gold-bearing material never left unattended; dual-key vault and logged exit

evidence.note: Concrete vault with a safe in the refinery (er2022).

steps.name: Crush the slag and return it to the mill
steps.description: The operator breaks up the stored slag and the magnetic reject, crushes them in the refinery jaw crusher, and returns them under escort to the ball mill feed so the gold prills are recovered.

evidence.note: Recycling slag to the mill is common in small refineries; frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the pour in the gold room and met records
steps.description: The operator types the batch type, sock press or table concentrate dates, ash or concentrate weight, flux, bar numbers and weights into the refinery spreadsheet and sends it to the metallurgist for the month's gold production.

error.defect_description: A bar weight is typed wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the gold room record goes to mill-met-accounting in the organisation file.

steps.name: Reconcile the pour with expected gold
steps.description: The metallurgist compares the poured bullion weight and estimated content with the gold expected from the period's pregnant and barren solution assays and flows, or from the table concentrate tonnage and grade, and flags any gap larger than the usual tolerance.

control.basis: Metallurgical accounting reconciliation of gold produced (internal control over reported production)

evidence.note: Reconciliation highlights larger losses (goldroom911); per-pour checks and the 5% flag rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate the gold difference
steps.description: The mill superintendent goes through the press change and burn logs, solution assays, gold room book, transfer sheets and scale records with the metallurgist, re-weighs bars if needed, and decides whether the gap is a sampling or recording error or a possible loss.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the refinery camera records
steps.description: The security officer pulls the CCTV recordings and access log for the press change, transfer and pour, checks each entry and handling step against the gold room book, and writes a short note for the mill superintendent.

evidence.note: CCTV in the refinery (er2022), with a 90-day recorder as common practice (goldroom911); review time is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Sock press change
exceptions.description: The loaded press is isolated, the socks are stripped under escort, burned overnight and the ash smelted.

exceptions.name: Unexplained gold difference
exceptions.description: The pour does not match expected gold; the superintendent investigates and security reviews camera records.

exceptions.name: Slag reprocessing
exceptions.description: Stored slag and magnetics are crushed and returned to the mill to recover gold prills.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from batch ready to bars in the vault
benchmarks.population: Small on-site refinery with one day-shift operator

evidence.note: Built from a wait of a few hours to two days for a refinery day, an overnight sock burn or concentrate drying and cooling, and a few hours to smelt, pour and finish; the author's estimate.
80-94% (er2022); 80-92% with silver at one part per six to ten parts gold (er2016).
Socks removed on a bi-weekly basis.

pain_points.description: Gold-bearing material waits in the vault for a refinery day and an overnight burn, which delays shipment and raises security exposure.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of batching.

pain_points.description: Every entry, press change, pour and weighing needs a second person, and the gold room operator waits for a security officer or the superintendent.
Opening a sock press exposes operators to cyanide solution and precipitate dust, so it needs lockout, draining and full PPE.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on the press design in er2022.

pain_points.description: Bar and ash weights are written by hand and re-typed into the refinery spreadsheet, and mismatches are found at reconciliation.

evidence.note: A hardcover gold room book records weights and conversions (goldroom911).

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (NI 43-101, SRK Consulting, 22 April 2022)
sources.supports: Section 17: mill permitted to 1,200 t/d on a crushing basis; three stockpile pads; loader feeds the jaw crusher, cone in closed circuit with a double-deck screen, fine ore bin, weightometer on the second mill feed conveyor; crushing product 80% passing 9/16 inch; primary and secondary ball mills with cyclones, 75% passing 74 um; semi-batch centrifugal gravity concentrator on cyclone feed, shaking table daily and magnetic separation; trash screen, pre-leach thickener (permanganate, flocculant, cyanide); six leach tanks (one standby), air sparged, 36-38 h retention, pH 10.5-11.2; drum filters; three clarifiers precoated with Dicalite and Solka Floc; vacuum towers, zinc dust and lead nitrate, sock presses with socks removed bi-weekly; tailings filtered on drum filters and conveyed for dry stacking; refinery with CCTV, vault, sock burner oven and propane Wabi furnace smelting table concentrate and burned sock ash to doré of 80-94% gold; hydrogen peroxide cyanide destruction in the Reclaim Pond; 2021-22 mill availability basis 93.3% (86% in 2021), average 779 t/d; recovery gravity 43%, Merrill-Crowe 88%, overall 97%; reagent use (NaCN 0.52 kg/t, lime 0.79 kg/t, zinc 0.086 kg/t). Sections 18.7 and 20.3: filtered tailings conveyed to stockpiles and redistributed by trucks and a dozer; Reclaim Pond feeds the mill; excess water treated to the Polishing Pond or stored in the Mishi pit; dam raises 2019 (Stage 3), 2020 (Stage 4) and 2022-24 (Stage 5); annual Dam Safety Inspections by consultants (SNC-Lavalin 2020, EXP 2021) under CDA guidelines, the Lakes and Rivers Improvement Act and MAC guidance; dams classed High; mill 17 km by road from the mine

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex (NI 43-101, G. Mannard and P. Ng, 17 March 2016)
sources.supports: Section 17: mill 17 km by road from the mine; Merrill-Crowe zinc precipitation with about 40% of gold to a Knelson gravity concentrate; precipitate refined on site to doré of 80-92% gold shipped to the Royal Canadian Mint; recovery about 95%; reclaim water reused; the mill runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week with crews on 12-hour shifts on a seven days in, seven days out rotation; practical limit about 1,050 t/d because of maintenance time

sources.title: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. - Environmental Compliance Approval (air), Eagle River Mill (ERO 012-8749)
sources.supports: Amended air approval of 21 December 2020 for the Eagle River Mill, 50 km west of Wawa: replacement of the laboratory fume hood and bullion furnace, a dicalite vent bin collection system, hydrogen cyanide emissions from the tailings pond and leach tanks, cyanide building and cyanide mixing ventilation; contaminants include hydrogen cyanide and zinc

sources.title: Gold Room Security
sources.supports: Double-locked single entry using card passes; CCTV with 90-day recorder and card access; permanent hardcover gold room book recording date, batch number, weights and conversions; very few people should know of pours or pickups; never leave cathode cake, gravity concentrate or smelted products unattended; insiders are historically the greatest threat; monthly metallurgical reconciliation highlights larger thefts

assumptions: The reference mill has no carbon elution or electrowinning: gold is recovered by gravity and by Merrill-Crowe zinc precipitation in sock presses, and the refinery smelts burned sock ash and shaking table concentrate (er2022, er2016). The organisation file's process name ('Carbon elution, electrowinning and doré pour'), its 'elution-circuit' resource and its 'loaded_carbon' object do not match this; the file keeps the process id and object id and adds a 'refinery' resource marked not_in_org_file.

A case is one smelt batch: one in three is a sock press change (about every two weeks) and two in three are weekly table concentrate smelts, about 6 batches a month against the organisation file's 6 to 10 strip and pour cycles.
Daily Merrill-Crowe operation (clarifiers, vacuum towers, zinc feed) is counted in mill-grind-leach; only the press change is here.
Bar samples go to the site assay lab; the organisation file has no link from this process to mill-assay-lab, so one is listed in interfaces.
Refinery running cost of C$20 to C$70 an hour (propane, crucibles, refractory and power) is the author's estimate; refractory liner use is 0.028 kg/t milled (er2022).

The gold room operator's stated 0.8 FTE is about twice the hands-on time in these steps; the rest is daily custody of table concentrate, vault counts, refinery housekeeping and standby while burns and drying run.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file.

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.
